blocks.text: Explanation:- Just as one should not interlock the fingers of one's hands in Salah, and doing so without need is not a desirable act, likewise it is improper for one who makes Wudu at home and comes to the masjid to pray. The reason is that, since he receives the reward of Salah, he becomes like one who is in Salah. This has been stated in detail in other narrations.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ مِنَ اْلأَنْصَارِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ: إِذَا تَوَضَّأَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ الْوُضُوءَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَي الصَّلَاةِ، لَمْ يَرْفَعْ قَدَمَهُ الْيُمْنَي إِلَّا كَتَبَ اللهُ لَهُ حَسَنَةً، وَلَمْ يَضَعْ قَدَمَهُ الْيُسْرَي إِلَّاحَطَّ اللهُ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَةً، فَلْيُقَرِّبْ أَحَدُكُمْ أَوْ لِيُبَعِّدْ، فَإِنْ أَتَي الْمَسْجِدَ فَصَلَّي فِي جَمَاعَةٍ غُفِرَ لَهُ، فَإِنْ أَتَي الْمَسْجِدَ وَقَدْ صَلَّوْا بَعْضاً وَبَقِيَ بَعْضٌ صَلَّي مَاأَدْرَكَ وَأَتَمَّ مَابَقِيَ، كَانَ كَذلِكَ، فَإِنْ أَتَي الْمَسْجِدَ وَقَدْ صَلَّوْا فَأَتَمَّ الصَّلَاةَ، كَانَ كَذلِكَ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه ابوداؤد باب ماجاء في الهدي في المشي الي الصلاة، رقم:٥٦٣
blocks.tamil_translation: “When one of you makes Wudu well and then goes to pray, every time he lifts his right foot Allah writes a good deed for him. For every step of the left foot that he puts down, He erases a bad deed. (Whether he takes small steps or long steps is his choice.) If he comes to the masjid and prays with the congregation, he is granted forgiveness. He comes to the masjid; the congregation is in progress; the people have prayed part of the Salah and part of the Salah still remains; if he prays the rak'ahs he gets (with the congregation) and then completes the rest alone, he too is granted forgiveness.
